title: Widow of King Oliver; Joe's family and birthplace Abbeville
summary: Stella introduces herself as Joe Oliver's widow, married 1912, and talks about both being born near Donaldsonville and his surviving sisters, including Mrs. Johnson in New York. A microphone and chair interruption occurs.

story.theme_name: Stating your name and birth date on tape
story.community_name: Opening the tape: name, birth date and birthplace

blocks.x: Well, I'm Stella Oliver, the widow of King Joe Oliver. We have been married, we married in 1912, July the 13th. Was a fine man, a fine husband, and a fine musician. We got along beautifully together. We traveled around, had our ups and downs together, but we still stuck. And I'm happy to say this morning that I'm, I'm glad to say a few words about Joe. He's dead now, nearly 18 years. He died 38. And I miss him quite a night. I miss him up until now. However, his name has lived in the public. He was a great musician and a great man. Everybody loved him. And I still love him too. Now, Joe was, I was born in Donisonville. A little place above, Abin where Joe was born. He was born in Abin. He's this brother, he has three sisters, no brother.
Or any of the brothers, or any of the other sisters, anyone else in the family living? Yes.
He has one sister in Arizona, and he has one in New York, and I think the one in Chicago died. I don't hear from him regularly now.
But the one in New York is still living?
Is still living, yes. Is that Mrs. Johnson? Mrs. Johnson, that's Mrs. Johnson, who he loved dearly. We lived with her about three years in New York.

Oh, excuse me for interrupting. Is that chair comfortable? I put the microphone on this side. Would you rather... Mrs. No, this is chair comfortable. Because I thought maybe you wanted to lean against the back more. Mrs. No, this is... Yes. Is that all right? Because we could put the microphone on the other side. Mrs. And then...
Excuse me if I'm interrupting. Mrs. That's all right. Well, if I'm not just right...
No, that's fine. I thought it wouldn't make it comfortable for you, though.
Mrs. Joe was born in Abin.
Is that on the other side of the river, or this side?
Mrs. That's on the other side. The other side.
